tei:bibl.tei:title: Con Gran Placer, Señores — a Western Sefaradi table-song for Purim
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: A very old Western Sephardic table-song, mentioned as early as the 18th century in Livorno and possibly even older, this ballad retelling the story of Purim is sung to the tune of “Akh Zeh Hayom Kiviti.” It is related to the briefer Haketia-language song “Haman mamzer el malo,” already found here. Also included are literal and singable English translations.

Note that this text is much closer to normative Spanish than Ladino as spoken in the Balkans. It could perhaps be considered a variant of Ḥaketia, the language of Tetouan, but this poem is old enough that there isn’t much of a practical difference.

This is a transcription of the Sefaradi table song for Purim, “Con Gran Placer, Señores,” largely as found in the Jewish Table Singing website of Jonathan Cohen, with variant forms from James Levy’s recording. Literal and singable English translations by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer.
My Friends, Let Me Inform You (Isaac Gantwerk Mayer, 2026)
